title: Tracon voice conversation frames
description: The JSON text frames of the voice conversation WebSocket (subprotocol tracon.voice.v1). Binary frames are raw audio and are not described here. A reader ignores a frame type and a property it does not know: new ones can be added without a new subprotocol.

ClientFrame.description: A text frame the client sends. Binary frames the client sends are audio of the utterance being spoken.

ServerFrame.description: A text frame the server sends. Binary frames the server sends are audio chunks of the answer, between an audioStart and an audioEnd.

Start.description: Starts the conversation. It is the first frame the client sends and it is sent once: the agent, the session and the tenant are fixed for the connection.

agent.description: The name of the agent to talk to.

voiceId.description: The voice the answers are spoken in. A host that set a connection resolver ignores it.

inputFormat.description: The audio the client sends: webm-opus (the default) or raw mono 16-bit little-endian pcm16.

Cancel.description: Barge-in: stop the answer that is being generated or spoken. While the client is listening it discards the audio gathered so far.

Ready.description: The server accepted start. The client may send audio.

persistAudio.description: Whether the audio of the answers is stored. Show it to the user: nothing is recorded silently.

Transcript.description: What the server heard. The text can be empty, and then the turn ends with an idle frame.

RunStarted.description: The agent's run started. The identifier is the run's, the one the run endpoints take.

Text.description: A piece of the answer, as a caption.

AudioStart.description: The binary frames that follow are audio chunks of the answer, in this media type.

AudioEnd.description: The audio chunks of one spoken sentence ended.

Error.description: Something went wrong. Before ready it ends the conversation; during a turn it ends the turn and a done frame follows.

Done.description: The turn ended, answered, interrupted or failed. An opening (a greeting or an opening prompt) ends with a done frame too, and its turn is 0.

cancelled.description: Whether the user interrupted the turn.

turn.description: The number of turns the user has completed.

attachmentId.description: The stored audio of the answer; absent when nothing was stored.

Idle.description: A commit closed no turn: it came before any audio, or the audio held nothing usable. The conversation is listening again. It is not an error and not a done.

Ended.description: The server ends the conversation and closes the socket right after this frame. The client does not reconnect on its own.

reason.description: agent: the agent ended the conversation after its answer. duration: the time limit the host set for this connection was reached; the turn in progress was cut off first. A reason you do not know means the same thing: the server ended the conversation, so do not reconnect.
